full_text: TO THE NATION. In  January 1932 the political situation in India was tense and explosive. The country was bubbling with enthusiasm of unprecedented intensity and people were bent upon casting away the yoke of slavery by hook or by crook. The Congress had already passed a resolu- tion   involving the  resumption of Civil Disobedience Movement and on the other hand, the British Govern- ment were bent upon suppressing the upheavals by all pos- sible means, and they had already apprised the Mahatma of their   intentions  through a telegram. At that critical period  Mahatma  Gandhi issued the following message to the Nation :—
